Run 48-hour pilot on 8k and 32k context model variants with sample dataset
action_items: Ethan Morales - Email pricing & latency matrix (due 2026-04-20)
Priya Nair - Draft pilot config and benchmark plan (due 2026-04-22)
Mark Dupree - Share sample dataset, current request/seq length distribution (due 2026-04-21)
Sofia Kim - Confirm decision timeline and budget (due 2026-04-24)
header: Date: 2026-04-18; Time: 14:00 PDT; Duration: 48 mins; Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (Acadia Head of ML), Mark (Platform), Sofia (CTO)
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for customer-facing assistants. Discussed context length needs (8k vs 32k), multilingual support, tool-calling/function-calling, and hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a short pilot and follow up with benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off in a minute. Quick intro from my side, I'm Ethan, AE for Redwood Inference, and Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi all, hey, quick agenda: model selection questions, context length, multilingual, and tool-calling requirements, then security questions at the end.
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks. We're looking to pick a model for our customer support assistant - needs to do routing, extract structured fields, call internal tools, and handle Spanish and French. Also some docs require 20k tokens-ish context.
[00:37] Mark Dupree: Right we have long conversation threads and we dump customer transcripts that are often 10-15k tokens, sometimes more. Primary constraint is latency under 1.2s 95th for short-turn responses, but long-context summarization can be higher.
[00:51] Sofia Kim: Security is a big deal - SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS for keys, and we need logs/audit trail.
[00:58] Ethan Morales: Totally, makes sense. Quick call out: on the model side you'll be choosing between hosted variants we provide, or Dedicated / Private if you want VPC or on-prem. For model families, do you have a preference for open models?
[01:12] Lena Ortiz: We prefer open models for auditability. Also we want function calling to invoke internal APIs (ticket create, account lookups) - is that supported?
[01:20] Priya Nair: Yes - Redwood supports tool/function calling semantics. There are two parts: the model needs to support structured output and we provide the runtime hooks to securely call customer tools (with routing and secrets). For Hosted we provide a secure connector, for Dedicated/Private you can run connectors in your VPC.
[01:36] Mark Dupree: For long context, can you do 32k? We tested some models on other clouds but the latency cost is killing us.
[01:44] Priya Nair: We have 8k, 16k, and 32k verified variants in our catalog. The tradeoff is compute per token and latency. For interactive short requests we'd route to lower-context cheaper models; for long-context summarization we route to 32k variants or use prefix/KV cache to avoid re-encoding the whole history.
[02:02] Lena Ortiz: Prefix/KV cache - can you explain that quickly?
[02:06] Priya Nair: Sure. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching so common conversation prefixes or document embeddings can be cached; that reduces the sent tokens and GPU work. For example, if you have a knowledge base doc that's 12k tokens, we can keep it in cache and only send the delta. It isn't magic but it helps cost and latency a lot.
[02:22] Mark Dupree: Okay that helps. What about multilingual quality - we need equal-ish quality in Spanish and French, and some Portuguese.
[02:29] Ethan Morales: For multilingual, model selection depends - some open families are stronger (XLM-like or multilingual LLMs), some fine-tuned English models degrade on other languages. We can run evals across your language prompts. Which languages/volumes?
[02:43] Lena Ortiz: Spanish heavy (about 40% of traffic), French 10%, Portuguese 5%. Rest English.
[02:49] Priya Nair: We'll propose a shortlist. Typically we'd test a few open models (we often recommend Mistral-based and Llama2/Alpaca variants depending on your safety profile), and compare against Anthropic/OpenAI if you want a hosted comparison. There will be a cost/latency delta.
[03:05] Sofia Kim: On security - for Dedicated vs Hosted, what's available? We can't have customer data leaving our VPC for regulated flows.
[03:13] Priya Nair: Dedicated can be deployed with VPC peering or a private network path; Private (on-prem) keeps everything customer-side with Redwood control plane in the customer account or an air-gapped option for regulated setups. Both support KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
[03:27] Mark Dupree: And SSO?
[03:29] Ethan Morales: SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported across plans; we can share our security pack (SOC2, penetration test summary, encryption at rest/in transit).
[03:39] Mark Dupree: Latency numbers - can you share ballpark for 8k vs 32k?
[03:43] Priya Nair: Ballpark: for similar hardware, 8k models have roughly 0.5-0.9s 95th for single-turn generation at our default tuning; 32k models often hit 1.2-1.8s depending on sequence length and batch. But we can pin dedicated capacity for predictable SLOs. Also quantized model variants can reduce cost but some latency tradeoff and possible quality regression.
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: We're leaning Hosted to start but want the option to move to Dedicated in 6 months.
[04:11] Ethan Morales: That's a common path. We can do a hosted pilot and give you migration playbooks for Dedicated. For the pilot we'll include an 8k and a 32k variant so you can compare quality and cost.
[04:22] Sofia Kim: About function-calling - do you provide tools to validate and sandbox the calls? We won't let arbitrary code hit our services.
[04:30] Priya Nair: Yes - we support a policy layer: white-listed endpoints, input validation, and a secure secrets connector. We can run an optional proxy in your VPC that inspects and vets calls.
[04:40] Mark Dupree: For benchmarking, what metrics should we capture? We want latency P50, P95, cost per 1k tokens, and hallucination/error rates on extraction tasks.
[04:49] Priya Nair: Agreed - also include language-specific accuracy, token distribution, and throughput under concurrent users. We'll help instrument with our tracing hooks and token-level cost reports.
[05:00] Lena Ortiz: One more on dev ergonomics - does Redwood support streaming and partial outputs? Our UI depends on streaming for perceived latency.
[05:07] Ethan Morales: Yes, streaming is supported in the API and we have SDKs for common stacks. That plus function-calling should cover your real-time flows.
[05:15] Sofia Kim: Any gotchas with model weights and licensing for open models? We need to ensure redistrib is compliant.
[05:22] Priya Nair: We'll include model license notes. Some open variants have non-commercial restrictions; we avoid those for production. We also offer Redwood-verified performance profiles for curated models.
[05:32] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Can you also include a cost estimate for routing strategy - send short interactions to cheaper variants and fall back to 32k for long context?
[05:40] Ethan Morales: Yep we'll produce a routing cost matrix. We'll simulate your sample traffic distribution once you share the dataset.
[05:47] Mark Dupree: I'll upload a redacted sample transcript set after the call.
[05:50] Priya Nair: Great. For the pilot we'll set up two routes, instrument metrics, and run head-to-head quality tests in Spanish/French.
[05:58] Sofia Kim: Timeline - we want pilot results in ~2 weeks, then a decision by the end of the month.
[06:04] Ethan Morales: Ok we'll aim for pilot kickoff within 3 business days.
[06:08] Lena Ortiz: Thanks, that's all from us.
[06:10] Ethan Morales: Thanks everyone. Recap in an email: pricing, pilot plan, security docs.
[06:16] [END]
